statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-0992: libxml2 traverses an XML catalog chain again for every repeated <nextCatalog> element that points to the same downstream catalog, so a crafted catalog causes excessive CPU use (https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/issues/1019). Debian fixed it for trixie in libxml2 2.12.7+dfsg+really2.9.14-2.1+deb13u3, whose changelog reads "Fix CVE-2026-0992: Denial of Service vulnerability due to uncontrolled resource consumption when processing XML catalogs containing repeated `<nextCatalog>` elements" (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-0992). The DHI libxml2 packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's trixie libxml2. The rebuilds of 2.12.7+dfsg+really2.9.14-2.1+deb13u2 predate the fix; the first rebuild of 2.12.7+dfsg+really2.9.14-2.1+deb13u3, used as the fixed version here, and every later build are built from that Debian release, and the Debian changelog shipped in the current libxml2 package (read for amd64 and arm64) carries Debian's entry for this CVE.
